plain_text:
Gestational diabetes is a disease
that develops during pregnancy and
affects how the body turns food into
energy. In the U.S., about 6% to 9% of
pregnant women develop gestational
diabetes. Women who develop it are at
increased risk for type 2 diabetes later
in life.
semantic_text: Gestational diabetes is a disease that develops during pregnancy and affects how the body turns food into energy. In the U.S., about 6% to 9% of pregnant women develop gestational diabetes. Women who develop it are at increased risk for type 2 diabetes later in life.

plain_text:
Cuilin Zhang, M.D., Ph.D., is a
clinical epidemiologist at the National
Institute of Child Health and Human
Development researching the genetic
and environmental factors that cause
gestational diabetes. She shares more
about the disease's lasting effects,
its link to type 2 diabetes, and her
research into prevention.

She shares more about the disease's lasting effects, its link to type 2 diabetes, and her research into prevention.

plain_text:
I was interested in gestational diabetes
because it's not just a pregnancy
complication, but it can impact the
fetus and the child. Children born
from pregnancies complicated by
gestational diabetes have an increased
risk for cardiometabolic disorders,
such as childhood obesity. After the
pregnancy, women, too, can have
exceptionally high risk of developing
type 2 diabetes and a greater risk of
cardiovascular diseases.

pregnancy, women, too, can have exceptionally high risk of developing type 2 diabetes and a greater risk of cardiovascular diseases.

plain_text:
I began my research on gestational
diabetes with a particular focus on
factors women can change that could
prevent the disease. We have also
researched potential biomarkers
[which can help predict disease]
you can change for early prediction
of gestational diabetes and to better
inform prevention and intervention.
semantic_text: I began my research on gestational diabetes with a particular focus on factors women can change that could prevent the disease. We have also researched potential biomarkers [which can help predict disease] you can change for early prediction of gestational diabetes and to better inform prevention and intervention.

plain_text:
Our research has looked at
gestational diabetes before
pregnancy, during pregnancy, and
after pregnancy. We discovered
that pre-pregnancy is a critical time
for gestational diabetes risk. We
identified a number of pre-pregnancy
factors that can impact this risk,
including smoking, a sedentary
lifestyle, unhealthy eating, and a body
mass index over 25. Not smoking,
exercising for more than 150 minutes
per week, eating a healthy diet, and
maintaining a healthy weight prior
to pregnancy was associated with an
83% lower risk of gestational diabetes.
semantic_text: Our research has looked at gestational diabetes before pregnancy, during pregnancy, and after pregnancy. We discovered that pre-pregnancy is a critical time for gestational diabetes risk. We identified a number of pre-pregnancy factors that can impact this risk, including smoking, a sedentary lifestyle, unhealthy eating, and a body mass index over 25. Not smoking, exercising for more than 150 minutes per week, eating a healthy diet, and maintaining a healthy weight prior to pregnancy was associated with an 83% lower risk of gestational diabetes.

plain_text:
Some of our current research
is looking into how gestational
diabetes can be predicted around
week 10 instead of around week 28
based on omics research tools such
as women's metabolome profiles.
This could allow us more time for
prevention and intervention.
semantic_text: Some of our current research is looking into how gestational diabetes can be predicted around week 10 instead of around week 28 based on omics research tools such as women's metabolome profiles. This could allow us more time for prevention and intervention.

plain_text:
Postpartum, we have identified a
number of healthful diet and lifestyle
factors that can help reduce the risk
of type 2 diabetes in women who have
had gestational diabetes. Some of these
include lactation [or breastfeeding]
and following a low carbohydrate, high
protein, and high fat diet mainly from
plant-sourced foods.

factors that can help reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes in women who have had gestational diabetes. Some of these include lactation [or breastfeeding] and following a low carbohydrate, high protein, and high fat diet mainly from plant-sourced foods.

plain_text:
Some people don't think that
gestational diabetes is a severe disease
because for a majority of women,
their glucose levels go back to normal
after pregnancy. Still, it can have
this long-term and lasting impact on
women's health and on the offspring's
health. It's important to think about
the health impacts of gestational
diabetes over their lifespan and the
implications it can have on children.

plain_text:
I hope that more research
focuses on understanding the
etiology, determinants, and health
consequences of gestational diabetes
in minority populations, as much of
the research has been done among
Caucasian populations. Minorities,
particularly Asian or Hispanic
women, are at much greater risk of
gestational diabetes.
